prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN)  -- The former Utah state trooper suspected in a series of roadway shootings earlier this week died Wednesday, the Dallas County Medical Examiner's Office said. CNN affiliate KSL in Salt Lake City, Utah, provided this file photo of the Dallas suspect, Brian Smith. Police said Tuesday that Brian Smith attempted suicide after Monday's shootings. Smith was brought to a local hospital in serious condition, officials said . At 7 p.m. Wednesday Smith died at Parkland Hospital, the medical examiner's office said. An autopsy is slated for Thursday. Two people were killed in the shootings along a three-mile stretch on and near the LBJ Freeway, about 10 miles northeast of downtown Dallas. Police used ballistic tests to link Smith, a 12-year veteran of the Utah state police, to three of the four shootings, Dallas Police Lt. Craig Miller said Tuesday. Miller said Smith was a suspect in both nonfatal shootings and one of the fatal shootings. He said it was unclear if Smith was a suspect in the fatal shooting that occurred first. The first attack occurred in the city of Garland at about 5:41 p.m. Victim Jorge Lopez, 20, was sitting in his Nissan at a traffic light in Garland when a man in a pickup pulled alongside him and fired shots into his car, killing him, Officer Joe Harn of the Garland police said. A few minutes later and two miles away on the LBJ Freeway, a gunman fired at two tractor-trailers. While one driver escaped injuries, William Scott Miller, 42, of Frankfort, Kentucky, was shot to death behind the wheel of a United Van Lines truck, police said. "He was going to be traveling home," Lt. Miller said. "He was about to park his rig. He was going to get on a plane to fly to be with his wife and children for the Christmas season and then come back to this location." Miller called the truck driver a hero because he was able to control his rig before he died -- preventing other motorists from being hurt. The fourth attack came a mile west on LBJ Freeway, where gunfire shattered the windshield of another tractor-trailer. The bullets missed the driver, but flying glass caused minor cuts, police said. Smith, 37, left his trooper job in Utah after he was caught abusing alcohol and drugs, CNN affiliate WFAA reported, citing an official report. The sergeant began using drugs and alcohol after his patrol car was rear-ended while he was writing a ticket, according to the report by Utah Peace Officers Standards and Training. He moved to Texas shortly afterward, the station said. Harn told WFAA that Smith's wife had phoned police Monday to say her husband was suicidal and driving around with a gun. Police were able to locate him using cell phone transmission towers. A three-hour stand-off followed, ending when Smith shot himself in the head, Harn said.

CNN affiliate KSL in Salt Lake City, Utah, supplied this file photograph of the Dallas suspect, Brian Smith. Police reported Tuesday that Smith had attempted suicide following Monday's shootings, after which he was transported to a local hospital in serious condition, officials said.

At 7 p.m. Wednesday, Smith died at Parkland Hospital, the medical examiner's office confirmed. An autopsy has been scheduled for Thursday.

Two people were killed during the shootings, which unfolded along a three-mile stretch on and near the LBJ Freeway, roughly 10 miles northeast of downtown Dallas. Police employed ballistic testing to connect Smith—a 12-year veteran of the Utah state police—to three of the four shootings, Dallas Police Lieutenant Craig Miller announced Tuesday.

Lt. Miller indicated that Smith was suspected in both nonfatal shootings as well as one of the fatal incidents. He noted, however, that it remained uncertain whether Smith was responsible for the first fatal shooting.

The initial attack took place in the city of Garland at approximately 5:41 p.m. The victim, 20-year-old Jorge Lopez, was seated in his Nissan at a traffic light when a man in a pickup truck pulled alongside and opened fire, killing him, according to Garland Police Officer Joe Harn.

Minutes later, roughly two miles away on the LBJ Freeway, a gunman targeted two tractor-trailers. While one driver escaped unharmed, 42-year-old William Scott Miller of Frankfort, Kentucky, was fatally shot behind the wheel of a United Van Lines truck, police reported.

"He was going to be traveling home," Lt. Miller said. "He was about to park his rig. He was going to get on a plane to fly to be with his wife and children for the Christmas season and then come back to this location." Lt. Miller praised the truck driver as a hero, noting that his ability to maintain control of the vehicle before succumbing to his injuries likely spared other motorists from harm.

The fourth attack occurred a mile further west on the LBJ Freeway, where gunfire shattered the windshield of another tractor-trailer. Although the bullets missed the driver, flying glass caused minor lacerations, police said.

Smith, 37, had resigned from his position as a Utah state trooper after being caught abusing alcohol and drugs, according to CNN affiliate WFAA, which cited an official report. Per the account from the Utah Peace Officers Standards and Training board, the sergeant began abusing substances after his patrol car was struck from behind while he was issuing a citation. **Report from Dallas: Ex-Utah Trooper Suspected in Deadly Highway Shootings Succumbs to Injuries**

According to the Dallas County Medical Examiner's Office, the former Utah state trooper linked to a string of highway shootings this week passed away on Wednesday. CNN's Salt Lake City affiliate, KSL, had earlier supplied an archival photograph of the suspect, identified as Brian Smith.

Authorities disclosed on Tuesday that Smith had turned a weapon on himself following Monday's shooting spree, arriving at a nearby hospital in critical condition. The medical examiner's office confirmed his death occurred around 7 p.m. Wednesday at Parkland Hospital, with an autopsy scheduled for the following day.

The violence claimed two lives across a three-mile corridor along the LBJ Freeway, situated roughly ten miles from Dallas's downtown core. According to Miller, Smith was implicated in both non-lethal attacks and one fatal shooting, though his connection to the first deadly incident remained uncertain.

The initial attack unfolded in Garland around 5:41 p.m., when 20-year-old Jorge Lopez was fatally shot while stopped at a traffic signal in his Nissan. Garland police officer Joe Harn explained that a driver in a pickup truck pulled beside Lopez's vehicle and opened fire.

Roughly two miles away on the LBJ Freeway, another shooting targeted two semi-trucks shortly thereafter. Though one driver emerged unharmed, 42-year-old William Scott Miller from Frankfort, Kentucky, died at the wheel of his United Van Lines truck. Lieutenant Miller noted that the victim had been nearing the end of his route, planning to fly home for a Christmas reunion with his family before returning to work. He praised the driver's actions in maintaining control of the truck despite his fatal wounds, crediting him with preventing additional casualties among nearby motorists.

A final shooting took place a mile further west, where gunfire shattered another truck's windshield. The driver avoided direct injury, though scattered glass fragments caused superficial wounds.

Citing an official document, CNN affiliate WFAA reported that 37-year-old Smith had resigned his Utah trooper position after being found guilty of substance abuse involving alcohol and drugs. Records from the Utah Peace Officers Standards and Training board indicated his substance use began following a rear-end collision with his patrol vehicle during a traffic stop. Shortly after leaving his position, Smith relocated to Texas.

Harn also told WFAA that Smith's wife had contacted police Monday, warning that her husband was suicidal and had left home armed while driving. Officers subsequently tracked his location via cell phone tower signals, leading to a three-hour standoff that concluded when Smith turned the gun on himself.
